strategies.name: Baseline Sequential 8-Stage All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Executes 8 all-reduce operations sequentially with local bidiagonal coupling and inverse coupling transformations between each stage. Total 8 all-reduce dispatches on full W*S vectors. Represents the straightforward reference implementation with no optimization—highest dispatch count but simplest control flow.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + AllGather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce into reduce-scatter (producing W shards) followed by all-gather, enabling local shard-wise bidiagonal transformations between the two phases. 16 total collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) on smaller payloads (S or W*S). Trades more dispatches for reduced per-rank communication volume and better load balancing.

strategies.name: Fused Bidiagonal-Coupling Inside Collectives
strategies.desc: Manually implements ring-based all-reduce using point-to-point primitives (if available) or reduce-scatter+allgather, fusing the bidiagonal coupling arithmetic directly into the reduction kernel. ~16-32 dispatches depending on ring implementation. Reduces memory traffic by eliminating intermediate full-vector materializations between coupling and reduction.

strategies.name: Two-Level Hierarchical Aggregation (Intra/Inter-Node)
strategies.desc: Exploits multi-node topology by performing 8 stages of intra-node reductions (across devices per node) followed by inter-node all-reduce, then broadcast back. Approximately 8*(2*num_nodes) dispatches on smaller payloads. Optimizes for network topology by overlapping fast NVLink/local operations with slower cross-node communication.

strategies.name: Pipelined Overlapping with Chunked Vectorization
strategies.desc:
Partitions the W*S vector into C chunks and pipelines all-reduce operations across chunks, allowing overlap of computation (bidiagonal transforms) with communication. Total ~8*C dispatches on W*S/C payloads plus local compute. Hides latency through parallelism but increases dispatch overhead—beneficial when compute/communication ratio is favorable.
